title: Boss: a week on the team
summary: Rejected pushes, a stale force push, a fork and a release: handle each the way a senior engineer would, and build the release tooling.

steps.title: The scene
body: Friday on a five-person team: the release goes out today. Since `v1.4.0` the team merged features and fixes,
a teammate keeps pushing while you work, and your terminal has a stray test tag in it.
The questions are the decisions. The three terminal steps are the release itself, in a real clone with a real
`origin`: write the notes from the log, get your last fix in although the push is rejected, and tag the release.

steps.prompt: Monday: `git push` is rejected (*fetch first*). You have 2 local commits, nothing pushed. The team wants linear history. What do you run?
steps.explain: Replay your unpushed commits on top of the teammate's work. Force would delete their commits; `reset --hard` would delete yours.

steps.prompt: Wednesday: you squashed your PR branch and ran `git push --force-with-lease`. It says *stale info*. Your reviewer mentioned they pushed a small fix to your branch. What next?
options: `git fetch`, cherry-pick or rebase their commit into your branch, then `git push --force-with-lease` again
Switch to `git push --force` so it goes through
Delete the remote branch and push again
Ignore it; the lease is advisory
steps.explain: The lease just saved the reviewer's commit. Bring it in, then push.

steps.title: Release notes from the log
prompt: The last release is the tag `v1.4.0` in `~/shop`. Write two files for the release announcement:
1. `~/answers/notes.md`: every commit since `v1.4.0` that is **not a merge**, oldest first, one per line as `- <subject>`.
2. `~/answers/authors.txt`: how many of those commits each person wrote, most first, as `git shortlog -sn` prints it.

checks.name: notes.md lists the commits since v1.4.0

hints: `v1.4.0..main` means "commits in main that are not in v1.4.0". `--no-merges` drops merge commits.
`--format='- %s'` prints each subject as a bullet; `--reverse` puts the oldest first.
`git shortlog -sn --no-merges v1.4.0..main > ~/answers/authors.txt` (`-s` counts only, `-n` sorts by count).
steps.explain: Release automation (release-please, semantic-release, GitHub's generated notes) does exactly this range query, then groups by commit type. That only works if the subjects are good, which is the real reason teams insist on Conventional Commits.

steps.title: Rejected, and the rebase conflicts
prompt: Your fix `fix: use the 21% VAT rate` in `~/shop` is not pushed yet, and `git push` is rejected: a teammate pushed `fix: use the reduced VAT rate` on the same line, plus a docs commit.

Finance confirmed that **21%** is right, so your line wins. Rebase your commit onto the server's `main`, resolve the conflict keeping `0.21m`, and push. No merge commit, and the teammate's docs commit must stay.
Careful: during a rebase **ours** is the branch you rebase onto (the teammate's side) and **theirs** is your commit being replayed.

checks.name: the server ends with your fix on top of the teammate's commits
checks.cmd: test "$(git -C /srv/git/shop.git log -1 --format=%s main)" = 'fix: use the 21% VAT rate' && git -C /srv/git/shop.git merge-base --is-ancestor "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/mate)" main
checks.fail: The server's `main` should have the teammate's commits, then yours on top.

checks.name: the VAT rate is 21%
checks.cmd: git -C /srv/git/shop.git show main:src/Vat.cs | grep -q '0.21m' && ! git -C /srv/git/shop.git show main:src/Vat.cs | grep -qE '^(<<<<<<<|=======|>>>>>>>)'
checks.fail: `src/Vat.cs` on the server should say `0.21m`, without conflict markers. In a rebase, your side is `--theirs`.

checks.name: no merge commit was added
checks.fail: A merge commit landed on `main`. Use `git pull --rebase`, not a plain `git pull`. Press Reset scenario.

checks.name: the rebase is finished and the tree is clean
checks.fail: A rebase is still in progress, or files are left over.

hints: `git pull --rebase` replays your commit on top of the teammate's and stops on the conflict in `src/Vat.cs`.
`git checkout --theirs src/Vat.cs` takes your version (theirs = the commit being replayed). Check with `cat src/Vat.cs`.
`git add src/Vat.cs`, then `GIT_EDITOR=true git rebase --continue` (keeps the message), then `git push`.
steps.explain: The ours/theirs swap trips up everyone once: a rebase checks out the upstream first and then applies your commits onto it, so "ours" is upstream. In a conflict like this one, also tell the teammate: their fix was overruled, and they should hear why from you, not from `git log`.

steps.title: Tag the release
prompt: Since `v1.4.0` the team shipped a feature and fixes (see `git log --oneline v1.4.0..main` in `~/shop`), so this release is a **minor** bump.
1. Tag the tip of `main` with the next version, as an annotated tag with the message `Release <version>` (for example `Release 1.9.0`).
2. Push **only** that tag. Your local test tag `try-me` must not reach the server.

checks.name: the server has an annotated v1.5.0 on main
checks.cmd: test "$(git -C /srv/git/shop.git cat-file -t v1.5.0 2>/dev/null)" = tag && test "$(git -C /srv/git/shop.git rev-parse 'v1.5.0^{commit}')" = "$(git -C /srv/git/shop.git rev-parse main)"
checks.fail: The server should have an annotated tag `v1.5.0` on `main`: a minor bump from `v1.4.0` because of the `feat:` commit.

checks.name: try-me stayed local
checks.fail: `try-me` reached the server: `git push --tags` pushes every tag. Delete it there with `git push origin --delete try-me`.

hints: `git push origin v1.5.0`. Check with `git ls-remote --tags origin`.
steps.explain: Push tags by name. `git push --follow-tags` is the safe shortcut: it pushes annotated tags that point at the commits being pushed, never stray lightweight ones like `try-me`.
